stem:
Krish is told that common salt forms when sodium and chlorine join chemically. The salt's taste and other properties differ from those of sodium and chlorine. He cannot separate sodium from the salt by sieving or filtering.

Which claim correctly classifies common salt?

options.text: Common salt is a compound because sodium and chlorine are chemically joined and its properties differ from theirs.
Common salt is a mixture because it is made from more than one element.
Common salt is a compound even if sodium and chlorine were only mixed and could be separated by sieving.
Common salt is a compound only because it looks white.

teacher.key_rationale: A compound has elements chemically joined, properties different from those elements, and no separation by physical methods. Calling salt a mixture, dropping the chemical-join condition, or judging from colour alone miss the hinge.
